deep_dive.title: How Correct Is Your Answer? A Semantic Correctness Framework for Open QA Evaluation
deep_dive.abstract: Reliable evaluation of open-ended question answering remains a bottleneck for measuring answer correctness of modern LLMs. Unlike multiple-choice tasks, free-form answers may be correct in many surface forms and may fail in qualitatively different ways, including incompleteness, contradiction, overgeneration, and endorsement of false premises. Existing judgment-based and similarity-based metrics often collapse these distinctions. We address this gap with three reusable contributions. First, we introduce a semantic correctness taxonomy that assigns open-ended answers to eight ordered classes, separating verbose-but-correct answers from those contaminated by hallucinated content. Second, we release CAP-Correctness, an 8.8k-example benchmark spanning widely used QA datasets, and CAP-Statements, an 11k-example dataset for converting question-answer pairs into declarative statements for natural language inference (NLI) training and statement-based evaluation. Third, we introduce CAP (Context-Aware Precision), a reference-based metric that scores question-conditioned statements using bidirectional NLI. Under a monotonicity protocol testing whether metrics respect the taxonomy's intended ordering, CAP outperforms established baselines.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Paper proposes an eight-class semantic correctness taxonomy for open QA, distinguishing complete, verbose, correct answers from hallucination-contaminated, contradictory, overgenerated ones, and releases CAP-Correctness 8.8k benchmark.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 开放域问答的正确性往往被一个分数掩盖，本文给出八个有序类的语义正确分类法，让冗长答案的正确内容与幻觉混入、矛盾、过度生成等失败不混淆。作者开放 CAP-Correctness 8.8k 标注样例用于衡量这些错误模式。评测视角从整体相似度转向结构化失败类型，为检验生成中的事实污染和覆盖面提供了认知明确的度量工具。
